note: Hand-labels written BEFORE any judge call. Based on recipe card knowledge (R001-R006) only, not on judge output. For OOC_REFUSAL mode: acceptable=true means the system correctly refused (refusal IS the correct response).
judge_binary_criterion: substitution is culinarily acceptable (function, method, flavour direction)

labels.reason: Almond flour introduces a tree-nut allergen not present in focaccia (R002). Protein too low for stretch-and-fold method. Doubly unacceptable: allergen-unsafe and structurally wrong.
Soy sauce introduces a soy allergen not present in R003. It disrupts the salt-to-pepper brine ratio (3.75%) required for safe lacto-fermentation at 21 C.
Rice flour is a documented GF substitute. Removes the gluten allergen from R005, which is an allergen safety improvement. Texture differs but substitution is safe and culinarily accepted.
Shrimp paste introduces shellfish allergen not present in kimchi (R004). Major new allergen added without equivalent in original recipe.
Red chili flakes share the same allergen class as gochugaru (none declared). Allergen-safe substitution; heat level will differ but no allergen risk.
Coconut oil is a known fat substitute in baking. Works in focaccia (R002) at same quantity. Flavour shifts to tropical-sweet; method remains intact.
Habanero peppers are in the capsicum family, just much hotter. Same fermentation behaviour and method. Sauce will be significantly hotter.
Commercial instant yeast cannot replicate a 24-hour sourdough fermentation. Lacks lactic acid bacteria for flavour development. R006 depends on LAB for its flavour profile.
Sweet smoked paprika has negligible heat vs gochugaru's 4000-8000 Scoville and a completely different flavour profile. Kimchi made with paprika tastes nothing like kimchi.
Whole milk in sourdough creates a known enriched-dough variant. Method (R001) remains compatible. Flavour direction is enriched-savoury, a recognised sourdough category.
Cake flour (7-9% protein) cannot develop gluten through stretch-and-fold. Focaccia (R002) will collapse into a flat, dense mass.
Kosher salt at same weight functions identically to fine sea salt in R001. Crystal size differs but dissolves fully during mixing. No method adjustment needed.
48 C kills sourdough starter organisms (die above ~40 C). The 24-hour fermentation in R006 becomes impossible. Dough will not rise.
Coil folds are the primary gluten-development mechanism in R005 (no-knead style). Skipping all folds produces weak, extensible dough. Baguettes will be dense and gummy.
Poolish at 100% hydration is a pre-ferment functionally analogous to sourdough starter. Equal weight provides comparable leavening. R001 method steps remain fully compatible.
Linear doubling: flour 2000g, water 1440g, starter 400g, salt 40g. All baker's percentages preserved. Method timing unchanged.
Linear halving from 500g to 250g flour: water 200g, olive oil 12.5g, salt 3.5g. All ratios preserved. Method unchanged.
Halving all baguette quantities gives 2 pieces of ~415g each. Method (R005) identical at half scale. Serving count correctly becomes 2.
Keeping 30g salt with only 300g jalapenos raises salt ratio from 3.75% to 10%. Too hostile for lactobacillus; batch will fail to ferment and be inedibly salty.
Tripling all kimchi quantities: cabbage 3600g, salt 180g, water 2700g, etc. All ratios preserved. Fermentation time unchanged.
